questions.q: What happened in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah?
questions.a: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

questions.q: Who did the king of Assyria send from Lachish to Jerusalem to Hezekiah?
questions.a: The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh.
He stopped at the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the Field of the Fuller.

questions.q: Who went out to meet the Rabshakeh?
questions.a: Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, the son of Asaph went out to meet the Rabshakeh.

questions.q: Who did the Rabshakeh say that Pharaoh, king of Egypt, was to anyone who trusted in him?
questions.a: The Rabshakeh said the Pharaoh was a splintered reed that if used as a walking stick would pierce your hand.

questions.q: What did the Rabshakeh say the king of Assyria would do if Hezekiah would make an agreement with the king of Assyria?
questions.a: The Rabshakeh said the king of Assyria would give Hezekiah two thousand horses.

questions.q: Who did the Rabshakeh say had told him to march against Judah and destroy it?
questions.a: The Rabshakeh said that Yahweh had told him to march against Judah and destroy it.

questions.q: Why did Eliakim, Shebna and Joah ask the Rabshakeh to speak to them in Aramaic?
questions.a: They did not want the people on the wall to hear and understand what was being said.

questions.q: Briefly, what did the Rabshakeh say were the words of the king of Assyria with regard to Hezekiah?
questions.a: He said not to let Hezekiah deceive them because Hezekiah would not be able to rescue them, and he said not to trust in Yahweh.

questions.q: How did the Rabshakeh respond to the request for him to speak to Eliakim, Shebna and Joah in Aramaic?
questions.a: He responded by standing and shouting in a loud voice in the Jew’s language, Judean.

questions.q: What did the king of Assyria say would happen if the Jews would make peace with him and come out to him?
questions.a: He said the Jews would eat from their own vine and from their own fig tree and drink water from their own well until he would come and take the Jews away to a land like their own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

questions.q: How did the king say that Hezekiah could mislead the Judean people?
questions.a: He said that Hezekiah could mislead them by telling them that Yahweh would deliver them.

questions.q: Did any of the gods deliver nations from the hand of the king of Assyria?
questions.a: No, none of the gods of those nations delivered them from the hand of the king of Assyria.

questions.q: What was the response to the Rabshakeh’s speech?
questions.a: They remained silent and did not respond, for the kings order was, “Do not answer him.”

questions.q: What did Eliakim, Shebna and Joah do after the Rabshakeh’s speech?
questions.a: They came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to Hezekiah the words of Rabshakeh.

commentary.text: See II Kin. 18:17-37, and the commentary thereon.
